title: EpistemicAtlas v3
description: A self-contained epistemic knowledge base for one real-world dispute (schema v3). The root object is a Case. v3 separates the reusable knowledge structure (sources, extracted_claims, normalized_claims, relations) from a more subjective assessment_layer (cruxes, failure_mode_flags, missing_evidence, assessments, reviews, audit_notes). Relations use a small set of families rather than a large fixed type vocabulary, and record how they are grounded via the basis field. The schema does not assert that any encoded case is authoritative: claims marked needs_source_verification have not been checked against primary sources, and the data_status field records the verification state of each case.

Case.description: The root container for one epistemic case study. A Case is a complete, self-contained JSON file. The core knowledge layer (sources, extracted_claims, normalized_claims, relations) is reusable and comparatively objective. The assessment_layer holds the more subjective interpretation built on top of it.

id.description: Unique kebab-case identifier for this case. Stable across versions.

schema_version.description: Must be '3' for this schema version.

domain.description: Primary knowledge domain (e.g., particle physics, nutrition science).

summary.description: Neutral 2-5 sentence description of the dispute. No position taken.

created.description: ISO 8601 date when this entry was first created.

updated.description: ISO 8601 date when this entry was last updated.

sources.description: All consulted sources. Low-credibility sources are included, not discarded -- their presence in the record is itself informative.

extracted_claims.description: Raw claims as they appear (verbatim or minimal paraphrase) in the source material. Extraction happens before normalization. Each ExtractedClaim belongs to exactly one Source.

normalized_claims.description: Standardized, unambiguous versions of claims. A NormalizedClaim may aggregate multiple ExtractedClaims from different sources that make the same proposition. This is where scope, quantification, and hedges are made explicit.

relations.description: Directed relationships between NormalizedClaims, grouped into a small set of families. The relation graph is the core epistemic structure of the case and is part of the reusable knowledge layer, distinct from the interpretation recorded in assessment_layer.

assessment_layer.description: The interpretive layer: cruxes, failure mode flags, missing evidence, one or more assessments, reviews, and audit notes. Separated from the core knowledge layer so the same sources/claims/relations can carry multiple, possibly disagreeing, assessments.

Source.description: A document, paper, statement, legal filing, or other artifact consulted during case construction. Provenance is captured in full regardless of source credibility.

id.description: Unique source identifier within this case. Convention: src_001, src_002, ...

provenance.description: Full provenance record. Use null for fields that are unknown, not omit them.

date.description: ISO date or year of publication.

credibility.description: Assessed credibility based on venue, methodology disclosure, and peer review status. High = peer-reviewed major venue or major institutional report with named methodology. Medium = working paper, news with named sources. Low = opinion, anonymous source, undisclosed funding conflict. Unknown = cannot be assessed.

conflict_of_interest.description: Known or suspected financial, institutional, or personal conflicts. Populate if known. Null if none detected.

retracted.description: True if this source has been formally retracted or significantly corrected.

needs_source_verification.description: True if the provenance metadata has not been verified against the actual source.

notes.description: Any additional notes about how this source should be used or interpreted.

ExtractedClaim.description: A claim as it appears in a source -- verbatim text or a minimal paraphrase that does not change meaning. No normalization, disambiguation, or scope-making happens at this stage. Multiple ExtractedClaims from different sources can feed into one NormalizedClaim.

id.description: Unique claim identifier. Convention: EC_001, EC_002, ...

source_id.description: ID of the Source this claim is drawn from.

raw_text.description: Verbatim text or minimal paraphrase. Preserve all hedges, quantifiers, and conditional language exactly as they appear.

location.description: Location within the source for traceability.

speaker.description: Named speaker or author if distinct from the source author (e.g., a quoted expert).

extraction_notes.description: Notes on why this claim was extracted or any ambiguity in the extraction.

needs_source_verification.description: True if this extracted text has not been checked against the primary source document.

NormalizedClaim.description: A standardized, unambiguous version of one or more ExtractedClaims. Normalization resolves ambiguous referents, makes scope and quantification explicit, and preserves hedges in the statement text. A NormalizedClaim that aggregates multiple ExtractedClaims represents a claim made independently by multiple sources -- its provenance strength is the union of its sources.

extracted_claim_ids.description: IDs of the ExtractedClaims this normalization is derived from. Multiple IDs indicate that different sources make the same proposition. At least one is required.

normalized_text.description: The standardized claim text. Explicit scope (who, what, when, under what conditions), quantification, and hedges should appear in the text itself, not only in metadata.

domain_type.description: What kind of claim this is. empirical = about observable states of affairs. theoretical = about models or mechanisms. methodological = about how to evaluate evidence. normative = about what should be. historical = about past states.

scope.description: Optional plain-language scope statement if the normalized text alone does not make scope fully explicit.

quantification.description: Optional plain-language quantification if the normalized text alone does not make it explicit.

hedges.description: List of epistemic hedges preserved from the source (e.g., 'may', 'suggests', 'is consistent with', 'preliminary evidence indicates'). A claim with hedges is not the same claim without them.

position.description: Position relative to the primary concern or risk framing of the dispute. pro = supports the concern. con = undermines the concern. neutral = relevant background. conditional = position depends on an unresolved crux. methodological = about how evidence should be evaluated.

level.description: high = directly supported by primary source data or established consensus. medium = supported by secondary evidence or expert opinion without direct primary data. low = contested, outdated, or from a methodologically weak source. speculative = theoretical extrapolation or very low credibility source.

notes.description: Explanation of the confidence level assignment. Required for non-obvious cases.

failure_mode_flag_ids.description: IDs of FailureModeFlag objects (in assessment_layer.failure_mode_flags) that apply to this specific claim.

needs_source_verification.description: True if the normalized form has not been checked against the underlying source text.

Relation.description: A directed relationship between two NormalizedClaims, grouped into a small set of families. Direction matters: 'A supports B' is not the same as 'B supports A'. v3 deliberately uses few families and pushes nuance into subtype, tags, basis, and notes rather than a large fixed vocabulary. The schema does not assume that logical 'support' and empirical 'evidence' are cleanly separable: both fall under the supports family and are distinguished, if needed, by subtype or tags. The basis field records how the relation is grounded (stated in a source vs. inferred by the annotator).

from_id.description: ID of the source NormalizedClaim in the relation.

to_id.description: ID of the target NormalizedClaim in the relation.

family.description: supports: A raises the credibility of B, whether by logical justification or empirical evidence. opposes: A lowers the credibility of B or stands in tension with it, covering contradiction, counter-evidence, and mutual tension. depends_on: A is only meaningful or true if B is true. contextualizes: A changes the scope or interpretation of B without simply supporting or opposing it, covering narrowing, generalizing, and reframing. equivalent: A and B assert the same proposition, typically from different sources.

subtype.description: Optional finer-grained label within the family, free text rather than a controlled vocabulary. Examples: 'logical', 'empirical', 'narrows', 'generalizes', 'reframes', 'mutual_tension', 'independent_restatement'. Use it to record nuance without forcing it into the family enum.

tags.description: Optional free-text tags for cross-case querying (e.g., 'empirical', 'kinematic_analogy').

basis.description: How this relation is grounded. asserted_in_source: a single source states the relation directly. asserted_by_later_source: a later source explicitly draws the connection between earlier claims. inferred_across_sources: the relation is synthesized by comparing multiple sources, none of which states it outright. analyst_inferred: the relation is the annotator's own logical inference, not stated by any source. unclear: the grounding has not been determined. This field lets a reader tell whether a relation reflects what a source said or what an annotator concluded.

basis_source_ids.description: If basis is asserted_in_source or asserted_by_later_source, the IDs of the Source(s) that assert the relation.

strength.description: strong = direct, logically tight, or methodologically robust. moderate = plausible and supported but involves inferential steps or methodological caveats. weak = indirect, speculative, or dependent on contestable premises.

notes.description: Explanation of the relation, especially for non-obvious cases or weak-strength relations.

Crux.description: A pivotal question or claim whose resolution would significantly shift the dispute. A crux is not just any contested claim -- it is specifically load-bearing for the overall dispute. If you resolved it one way, one major position is weakened; the other way, the opposing position is weakened. Aim for 2-5 per case. Lives in the assessment_layer because identifying a crux is an interpretive act.

statement.description: A single clear question or testable proposition. Prefer the yes/no question form.

description.description: Why this is a crux: what changes if it resolves true vs. false, and which claims become well-supported or undermined in each case.

dependent_normalized_claim_ids.description: IDs of NormalizedClaims whose validity depends on this crux.

status.description: Current resolution status. empirically_underdetermined = the evidence needed to resolve it does not yet exist. theoretically_underdetermined = the theoretical framework needed to evaluate it is not established.

resolution_notes.description: If resolved, explain how and by what evidence.

resolution_source_ids.description: IDs of Sources that provide the resolution evidence.

triggers.description: Optional workflow passes this crux suggests revisiting. Supports a living, nonlinear workflow rather than a one-time linear pipeline.

FailureModeFlag.description: A first-class annotation recording an epistemic failure mode at the specific location where it occurs. Flags attach to NormalizedClaims, Sources, or Relations -- not to the case as a whole. This enables cross-case queries like: which claims in industry-funded sources show source_incentive_pressure? Lives in the assessment_layer.

type.description: correlated_evidence_treated_as_independent: multiple observations treated as independent confirmation when they share a common source, method, or theoretical dependency. rhetorical_weight_exceeds_evidence: the forcefulness or frequency of a claim's assertion carries more argumentative weight than the underlying evidence justifies. hidden_assumption: the argument requires a premise that is not stated and would itself require justification. source_incentive_pressure: the source has financial, institutional, or reputational incentives to reach a particular conclusion that align with its stated conclusion. proxy_measure_problem: the study measures a variable that is used as a proxy for the true quantity of interest, without establishing that the proxy is valid. population_heterogeneity: a claim about a population is applied without accounting for meaningful sub-population differences that affect the conclusion. temporal_drift: conditions relevant to the claim have changed since the evidence was collected, reducing its applicability. closed_case_overconfidence: a claim treats a question as settled when significant uncertainty or legitimate dissent remains. vague_question: the question being answered is not well-defined, and different reasonable interpretations would yield different answers. analogy_dependency: the argument's force depends on an analogy whose validity is not established. direct_evidence_absent: the conclusion goes beyond what direct evidence supports, relying entirely on inference, model output, or indirect indicators. expert_consensus_without_dependency_map: citing expert consensus as evidence without identifying what that consensus depends on, making it impossible to assess whether the consensus should be revised in light of new evidence.

description.description: Specific explanation of how this failure mode manifests in this particular case. Not a generic definition -- a precise account of the instance.

applies_to_id.description: The ID of the object this flag applies to.

applies_to_type.description: What type of object is being flagged.

severity.description: critical = this failure mode significantly undermines the claim or source's contribution to the case. significant = meaningful weakness that should be weighed. minor = present but does not substantially change the epistemic status.

affects_conclusion.description: True if this failure mode, if taken seriously, would change the overall assessment.

Assessment.description: One epistemic assessment over the shared knowledge structure. v3 allows multiple assessments (e.g., from different assessors or perspectives) to coexist in assessment_layer.assessments, so the subjective interpretation is separated from the reusable sources/claims/relations layer. Each assessment must remain consistent with the claim and relation data it cites: if it calls a claim well-supported, there should be no strong unaddressed opposing relations on it.

author.description: Who produced this assessment. Null if anonymous or not recorded.

assessor.description: Optional distinct assessor identity, if tracked separately from author.

perspective.description: The standpoint this assessment is written from (e.g., 'primary builder', 'adversarial reviewer', 'domain expert').

assessment_scope.description: What this assessment covers if it is not the whole case (e.g., 'only the diabetic-subgroup sub-question').

summary.description: Short plain-language summary of this assessment.

status.description: settled = the central question has a clear resolution supported by strong, multiply-verified evidence. unsettled = significant genuine uncertainty remains. partially_settled = some sub-questions are resolved but the overall dispute is not.

settled_direction.description: If status is settled or partially_settled, a plain-language statement of the conclusion and what it is settled on.

epistemic_status_summary.description: Plain-language summary of the overall epistemic state for a non-specialist reader.

confidence.description: Optional overall confidence in this assessment, plain language.

crux_ids.description: IDs of cruxes this assessment treats as relevant.

key_crux_ids.description: IDs of the cruxes that are most load-bearing for this assessment. Should be a subset of the case's cruxes.

failure_mode_flag_ids.description: IDs of FailureModeFlags this assessment weighs most heavily.

missing_evidence_ids.description: IDs of MissingEvidence items this assessment treats as most consequential.

weak_link_ids.description: IDs of NormalizedClaims that are the weakest links in the dominant argument -- claims with meaningful failure flags or low confidence that the argument significantly depends on.

sensitivity.description: How robust this assessment's conclusion is to specific claims or cruxes being overturned. A light sensitivity analysis rather than a formal one.

target_id.description: ID of a NormalizedClaim, Crux, or weak link this sensitivity entry is about.

robustness.description: robust = the conclusion survives if this element is overturned. fragile = the conclusion changes if this element is overturned. unknown = not yet determined.

effect_if_overturned.description: What happens to the assessment if target_id is overturned or reversed.

what_would_update.description: Explicit scenarios that would change this assessment. The forward-looking question: what evidence or events, if they occurred, would require revising the conclusion? Each entry must specify what would be affected and how.

scenario.description: Plain-language description of the evidence or event.

would_affect_ids.description: IDs of NormalizedClaims or Cruxes that would be affected.

direction.description: strengthen = would increase confidence in the current assessment. weaken = would decrease confidence. resolve = would convert an unsettled crux to a settled one.

magnitude.description: decisive = would change the assessment status. significant = would change confidence levels substantially. minor = would refine but not reverse.

well_supported_claim_ids.description: NormalizedClaim IDs with high or medium confidence and no significant unaddressed opposing relations.

contested_claim_ids.description: NormalizedClaim IDs that remain genuinely contested.

dominant_failure_modes.description: Failure mode types (from the FailureModeFlag vocabulary) that appear most significantly across this case.

disagrees_with.description: IDs of other Assessments or Reviews this assessment disagrees with.

disagreement_notes.description: Explanation of where and why this assessment diverges from the ones in disagrees_with.

date.description: ISO date this assessment was produced.

notes.description: Additional assessment notes not captured elsewhere.

Review.description: An adversarial or multi-user review of the case or of a specific assessment. Reviews let more than one person scrutinize the same shared knowledge structure without overwriting each other's work, supporting multi-user and adversarial evaluation.

role.description: The reviewer's relationship to the entry. adversary = explicitly trying to break the entry. domain_expert = subject-matter check. builder = someone who built the entry reviewing their own work. collaborator = a co-author. other = anything else.

stance.description: Optional one-line stance (e.g., 'concurs with primary assessment', 'dissents on the settled status').

dissents_from_ids.description: IDs of Assessments, NormalizedClaims, Relations, or Cruxes this review dissents from.

MissingEvidence.description: Evidence that does not currently exist in any accessible form but whose existence would change the epistemic status of at least one crux or normalized claim. This is different from evidence that exists but was not cited, or evidence that one party has withheld. Lives in the assessment_layer.

description.description: What the missing evidence is and why it is absent.

type.description: empirical = a study or measurement that has not been done. theoretical = a derivation or proof not established. historical = a record that may have existed but is inaccessible. legal_institutional = documentation not publicly released.

would_affect_ids.description: IDs of NormalizedClaims or Cruxes that this evidence would affect.

priority.description: critical = its absence directly prevents resolution of a key crux. important = would substantially clarify the dispute. helpful = would add precision but is not blocking.

reason_absent.description: Why this evidence does not exist: not yet studied, technically infeasible, ethically prohibited, access restricted, etc.

feasibility.description: Whether this evidence could in principle be obtained.

triggers.description: Optional workflow passes this missing-evidence item suggests revisiting if the evidence becomes available.

AuditNote.description: An adversarial review annotation. AuditNotes record issues found during the review step -- problems with normalization, source gaps, asymmetric flagging, etc. Each note has a resolution status so the audit log remains live. Lives in the assessment_layer.

type.description: normalization_concern = normalized form may have changed the meaning of the raw claim. source_gap = significant source, perspective, or evidence was not consulted. asymmetric_flagging = failure flags applied inconsistently across positions. relation_error = a relation is mis-directed, wrong family, or missing. crux_quality = identified crux is not actually load-bearing, or a real crux was missed. missing_evidence_framing = missing evidence is framed in a way that favors one side. assessment_inconsistency = the assessment contradicts claim or relation data. verification_needed = a specific claim requires primary source verification. llm_artifact = a claim, source reference, or relation may have been generated by an LLM without grounding in actual source text. other = does not fit above categories.

applies_to_ids.description: IDs of objects this note applies to.

status.description: open = issue has not been addressed. resolved = a correction was made. dismissed = reviewed and decided not to correct, with reason in resolution field.

resolution.description: How the issue was resolved, or why it was dismissed.

triggers.description: Optional workflow passes this audit note suggests revisiting.

AssessmentLayer.description: The interpretive layer, separated from the reusable knowledge structure (sources, extracted_claims, normalized_claims, relations). Everything here is more subjective and may be revised, contested, or duplicated across assessors. Cruxes, failure mode flags, missing evidence, assessments, reviews, and audit notes all reference the core layer by ID.

cruxes.description: Pivotal questions whose resolution would significantly shift the dispute.

failure_mode_flags.description: Epistemic failure mode annotations attached to specific claims, sources, or relations.

missing_evidence.description: Evidence that does not currently exist but whose existence would change the status of a crux or claim.

assessments.description: One or more assessments over the same knowledge structure. Multiple assessments support adversarial or multi-perspective evaluation; a single-assessor entry has exactly one.

reviews.description: Adversarial or multi-user reviews. May be empty when no separate review has been performed.

audit_notes.description: Adversarial review annotations with resolution status.

WorkflowTrigger.description: A workflow pass that an item suggests revisiting. Supports a living, nonlinear workflow: a new crux, a piece of missing evidence, an audit note, or a new source can trigger another pass rather than a one-time linear pipeline. rescope = revisit the case question. reingest = consult or add sources. reextract = re-extract claims. renormalize = re-normalize claims. remap_relations = revisit the relation graph. reassess = redo the assessment. re_review = run another adversarial review.

DataStatus.description: verified = all claims checked against primary sources. partial = some verified, some not. sample = illustrative only, treat as a demonstration of schema structure.
